sections.html:
A Sierra Vista owner can hire an agent, go it alone, or accept a cash offer on the house as it stands. Your closing deadline and the amount of work the house needs usually point to one of them.

One thing sets this market apart. Fort Huachuca, the Army post at the northwest edge of town, creates a steady rhythm of arrivals and departures. If a permanent change of station, a deployment or a family move sets your deadline, ask each buyer for a written closing date as well as a price.

The city has about 44,907 residents, which is 0.9 percent below the April 2020 estimates base of 45,310. The population is flat, so price against recent local sales instead of expecting a rush of new buyers. Owner-occupants hold 62.0 percent of homes. With nearly four in ten households renting, landlords and investors also bid on houses here.

Before you call anyone, write down your payoff balance, the repairs you already know about, and the date you need the money. Those three items let a buyer quote you a real number the same day and keep the conversation from dragging on.

A typical owner-occupied home is valued at $254,200, and typical gross rent is $1,150. The city has 18,862 households of 2.29 people on average, earning a median of $70,291. Home values here are well below the Phoenix-area cities.

Sierra Vista is the commercial center of Cochise County, about 75 miles southeast of Tucson, with State Routes 90 and 92 as the main roads. Nearly half of local jobs are government jobs, and Army contracts support a large professional and technical sector. The average commute is 17.5 minutes, which is worth mentioning in a listing.

The Sierra Vista Unified School District operates Buena High School, one middle school and six elementary schools. Cochise College and the University of Arizona College of Applied Science and Technology offer higher education nearby.

Questions about repairs go to Community Development at (520) 417-4413. Call before you assume a project is exempt from a permit. The city asks for plans as one complete, editable PDF with no passwords. Work in the public right-of-way and pool or spa drain applications go to the Public Works Department, and home-based business permits run through the City Clerk.

Landlords should understand how the city treats rental income. The city property tax rate is $0.1056 per $100 of assessed value and the sales tax rate is 1.95 percent. An owner who hires a management company can operate under that company's city business license. An owner who manages the house personally and must collect and remit real property rental tax needs a city business license of their own. Sierra Vista is a program city, so the Arizona Department of Revenue collects the privilege taxes, and the city cannot give binding tax opinions.

A separate state statute, A.R.S. 9-500.39, narrows what cities may impose on short-term rentals. A permit fee is capped at $250 or the actual cost, and proof of $500,000 in liability coverage can be required. If your buyer plans nightly rentals, the City Clerk can say whether a permit applies.

Deeds are filed with the Cochise County Recorder. Every deed needs a completed affidavit of property value attached (A.R.S. 11-1133). Without one, the recorder must turn the deed away, unless it cites an exemption under A.R.S. 11-1134. Exempt transfers include:

  • A deed of gift
  • A conveyance carried out under a court order
  • A nominal-consideration transfer among parent and child, spouses, or siblings

Recording costs $30 per instrument (A.R.S. 11-475). The Recorder can explain the current mail-in and electronic filing options, and your title company will put the total on the closing statement.

After recording, the Cochise County Assessor updates the owner name on the tax roll. A tax notice that still arrives for the former owner should go back to the Treasurer at P.O. Box 1778, Bisbee, AZ 85603, marked as sold.

Closing typically follows this order: you accept an offer, the title company searches the record for liens, both sides sign, and the deed is sent to the Recorder. Having your mortgage payoff figure, any tax notice and any permit paperwork ready shortens the middle step. If a tenant lives in the house, bring the lease to the title office as well, because the buyer will want to see the rent and term.

Cochise County sends one combined bill covering the city, county, schools, college and special districts, payable in two installments. Bills are mailed in September. If none has come by October 10, phone the county, since the obligation exists even when the notice is lost.

InstallmentDueDelinquent after 5:00 p.m.
First halfOctober 1November 1
Second halfMarch 1May 1
Total bill of $100 or lessOctober 1, in fullDecember 31

A due date on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day (A.R.S. 42-18052).

Once a date passes, simple interest runs at 16 percent a year, charged as 1.333 percent a month. Taxes still unpaid after May 1 and into the following January pick up a further 5 percent penalty, and the county sells its lien on delinquent parcels each February.

Each January the tax lien attaches to the parcel regardless of the owner, so get a current balance from the Treasurer before signing a contract. A title company can settle whatever is owed out of your proceeds at closing and keep the schedule intact.

If you think your value is wrong, an appeal concerns the property's value and starts when the notice of value arrives. Contact the Cochise County Assessor for that process.

Some cash buyers accept a house with a tax balance and simply lower the offer by that amount. This can be easier than paying first, but compare the net number against what a listing would leave you. Delinquent taxes grow every month at the interest rate above, so do not let the balance sit while you decide.

faqs.q: Does Fort Huachuca affect how fast a Sierra Vista house sells?
faqs.a: It affects who is looking. The post is the city's main employer, and nearly half of local jobs are in government. Shape your price and timeline around that, and get a closing date in writing.

faqs.q: Do I need a city business license to rent my Sierra Vista house?
faqs.a: It depends on who manages the rental. A property management company can operate under its own city license. If you manage it and must collect and remit real property rental tax, you need your own. Call Community Development or the City Clerk to confirm.

faqs.q: What does it cost to record a deed in Cochise County?
faqs.a: State statute A.R.S. 11-475 fixes recording at $30 per instrument; copies are $1 per page and a certificate is $3. The Recorder or your title company can give current steps and any extra charges.

faqs.q: What happens if my Cochise County taxes are delinquent when I sell?
faqs.a: The unpaid amount carries interest at 16 percent a year and may be sold as a lien in February. Request a payoff figure from the Treasurer and let the title company pay it when you close.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Sierra Vista house without repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, you can sell as-is, since the state mandates no repairs. Buyers with a mortgage may press for fixes after an inspection, whereas cash buyers price the work into their offer. Raise any unpermitted work with Community Development at (520) 417-4413 before you list.
